$comment: SHARED configuration for the tscircuit workspace, committed to main: facts whose value is the same in every developer's copy. Anything that describes one developer's current work (which patch-set effort they are running, personal overrides) belongs in .local/workspace.local.json instead, which is versioned on an orphan branch pushed only to their fork and deep-merged over this file. Plain JSON (not JSONC) so `node -e` can read it with no dependency; explanatory text lives in `description` fields, which the tooling prints, rather than in comments nothing can see. See `./tsc-dev config` for the effective merge.

$repoNotes: One line per repo, rendered into MAP.md by `./tsc-dev gen-map`. Keep them short: what the package IS, not how to use it.

repoNotes.eval: transpiles + evaluates TSX to Circuit JSON (in a web worker)
repoNotes.runframe: React preview UI (PCB/schematic/3D), runs eval in a worker
repoNotes.props: zod prop schemas for every component
repoNotes.circuit-json: the low-level data format everything speaks
repoNotes.circuit-to-svg: Circuit JSON to schematic/PCB/assembly SVG (used everywhere, incl. snapshot tests)
repoNotes.circuit-to-canvas: Circuit JSON to a canvas renderer
repoNotes.circuit-json-to-gltf: glTF scene for 3D preview and export
repoNotes.capacity-autorouter: capacity-based routing strategy used by it
repoNotes.dsn-converter: Specctra DSN in/out for external routers
repoNotes.schematic-match-adapt: fit a schematic to a known template
repoNotes.circuit-json-to-tscircuit: Circuit JSON back into TSX source

bundling.description: Which packages are baked into which other packages at BUILD time. tscircuit packages are inlined, not resolved from node_modules at runtime: core/props/circuit-json are bundled into eval's webworker, that worker is base64-embedded into runframe's standalone.min.js, and the cli serves that bundle. So a change is invisible downstream until every level below it is rebuilt, bottom-up — `./tsc-dev rebuild --from <repo>` computes that order from this graph. Read each entry as 'consumer: packages baked into it'. The graph is advisory and deliberately a superset of literal inlining (rebuilding one level too many is harmless; one level too few silently ships a stale bundle) — edges are verified against the consumer's real package.json at run time, and edges to repos you have not cloned are skipped.

build.description: How a local build is performed, and what counts as one of its inputs. `profiles` says what a build DOES: 'full' is exactly what the repo's own CI runs (always used by publish, pr-check, and anything that leaves this machine), 'dev' is the inner loop — declaration emit dropped (61% of a full chain rebuild, and neither the browser nor `tsci build` reads a byte of it) and any step the local dev server does not serve skipped. `inputs` says what a build READS: one declaration used by BOTH the watchers (do not rebuild on a file the build ignores) and the action key (hash exactly what a rebuild depends on), because maintaining those separately drifts invisibly in both directions. The defaults live in bin/build-inputs.mjs and exclude tests, docs and build output; add patterns here only when a repo genuinely differs, and prefer over-inclusion — an over-narrow input set fails SILENTLY by shipping a stale bundle.

cache.description: Local content-addressed store of build artifacts, keyed by the action key. Set TSC_DEV_NO_CACHE=1 to bypass it, TSC_DEV_CACHE_DIR to move it; `./tsc-dev cache status|prune|verify` inspects it.
